instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl, changing the water until it runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 1 3/4 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to the lowest setting. Cook for 15 minutes. Leave the lid on and let it sit off the heat for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces and pat them dry. Transfer them to a bowl, sprinkle over the 1/2 tsp salt and add the 1/3 cup cornstarch. Toss until every piece is coated.
Grate the garlic. In a small bowl, stir together the garlic, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp of the honey and 2 tbsp water. This is the glaze.
In another small bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, the remaining 1 tsp honey and the rice vinegar. Slice the green onions and tear the seaweed into small pieces.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high for 2 minutes, until a piece of chicken sizzles right away when it goes in. Add half the chicken in a single layer. Cook for 4 minutes without moving it, until the underside is deep golden and lets go of the pan. Flip the pieces and cook the other side for 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels. Cook the second batch the same way.
You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when the juices run clear.

Pour off the oil, leaving a thin film in the skillet. Turn the heat to medium, add the glaze and let it bubble for 1 minute, until it turns syrupy. Add the chicken and toss for 30 seconds, until every piece is glossy. Take the pan off the heat.
Taste a piece of chicken. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Divide the rice between 4 bowls. Top with the chicken, drizzle over the mayo, and scatter the seaweed, green onions and sesame seeds. Serve with the gochujang on the side, for stirring into your own mayo.

To pack it for lunch: pack the rice and chicken in one container and the mayo and seaweed in small separate containers. It keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat the chicken and rice in the microwave for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the mayo and seaweed. For crisper chicken, warm it in a 400°F oven or air fryer for 5 minutes.
method_notes: No version I could read had a rating on its page, so this is a fallback and the lead is a weak one: the Kewpie gochujang mayo chicken bowl, which is crispy cornstarch chicken, a mayo sauce, seaweed and rice. Cook with Juyea has the soy glaze, seaweed and mayo over rice but uses shredded cooked chicken, and Great British Chefs has a soy and honey glaze. I combined them: crispy thigh pieces, a soy and honey glaze, and a plain mayo sauce with the gochujang moved to the table so the base stays mild.
